items.title: William Russell Interview, 1962-09-04
items.q: Probably Tubby Hall and the pianist was another Alexander. I can't think of his first name, but it wasn't Charlie Alexander who had played with him on some of the early records.

ctx.x: Yes. Right at the end of the line. You go to the end of the line and this place, the One Cent Club, it means that you buy one drink at the regular price and you get a second drink for one cent. It was during the Depression, of course. They had on big blue silk blouses with big long full sleeves, you know, sort of like clowns wear. Not that they were trying to make clowns out of them, but I mean, it was a special uniform they wore. A drummer, I believe it must have been, I'm not sure, unless I, until I look up my…
I heard that song as a white religious piece.

items.title: William Russell Interview, 1962-08-31
items.q: I first heard him, oh, maybe half a dozen times on the south side with Johnny Dodd's band... I wouldn't have hardly known who he was at that time when Johnny first introduced me.

ctx.x: Now these are typed in the back of the Defender notes.

Yeah. That's some of the later Defender notes, some things that I probably didn't get. He probably looked through my notes and then went up there and went through a couple of years. We'll copy all this stuff for you. So in any case, there are a few other interviews, people that are dead there like Tubby Hall and Joe Lindsay. Unfortunately, we got very little bit from Tubby Hall. I wanted to apologize on that. He was one of the great drummers, I'm convinced the more I hear of other drummers especially. At that…
